To check disk space in Linux, you can use the `df` command. This command reports total disk space, used disk space, and free disk space on all mounted regular file systems (Page 499). 

For example:
```bash
df -h
```
This will display the disk space usage in a human-readable format.

Additionally, you can use the `lsblk` command to list details of block devices, including their size and UUID (Page 499). For example:
```bash
lsblk
```
This provides a tree view of block devices and their mount points.
